content.user_title: Build Azure AI Agents in Java
content.value_statement: Building persistent Azure AI agents in Java requires several SDK concepts. This skill gives concise setup, authentication, workflow, and cleanup guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains the Maven dependency for the Azure AI Agents Persistent SDK.
Shows required project endpoint and model deployment environment settings.
Demonstrates DefaultAzureCredential client setup for Java applications.
Outlines agent, thread, message, run, response, and cleanup steps.
Summarizes polling, error handling, cleanup, and async client guidance.
limitations: Does not create Azure resources or assign cloud permissions.
Requires a valid Azure AI project endpoint and model deployment.
Uses SDK examples that may need updates for newer package versions.
Does not replace application testing or security review.

use_cases.title: Prototype an agent workflow
use_cases.description: Map the basic Java steps for creating an agent, thread, message, run, and response flow.

use_cases.title: Review Azure integration steps
use_cases.description: Check authentication, endpoint configuration, and lifecycle cleanup before adding the SDK to a service.

use_cases.title: Prepare team implementation notes
use_cases.description: Turn SDK concepts into practical guidance for developers who maintain agent-backed Java applications.

prompt_templates.title: Set up the SDK
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to add the Azure AI Agents Persistent SDK to a Java project and configure the required environment values.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through creating an Azure AI agent, thread, user message, run, response retrieval, and cleanup in Java.

prompt_templates.title: Plan error handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Java agent workflow and list the run statuses, exceptions, and cleanup paths I should handle.

prompt_templates.title: Design production usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production checklist for using Azure AI Agents Persistent SDK in a Java service with async clients and controlled polling.

output_examples.input: I need to create a persistent Azure AI agent from a Java service.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step workflow covering dependency setup, endpoint configuration, client authentication, agent creation, thread messaging, run polling, and cleanup.

output_examples.input: I am unsure which run states and failures my service should handle.
output_examples.output: A review checklist covering queued and in-progress polling, action-required states, failures, cancellation, timeout behavior, and resource cleanup.

output_examples.input: My team needs concise guidance for Azure AI agent lifecycle management.
output_examples.output: A practical summary of agent, thread, message, run, response, and deletion responsibilities for Java maintainers.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential with managed identity or approved local credentials.
Poll run status with controlled intervals and timeout handling.
Delete temporary threads and agents when they are no longer needed.
anti_patterns: Hard-code endpoints, deployment names, or credentials in source files.
Assume every run completes without checking failed or canceled states.
Leave temporary agent resources active after tests or demos finish.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps plan Java applications that use Azure AI Agents Persistent SDK workflows.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources for me?
faq.answer: No. You must provide the Azure AI project, model deployment, permissions, and endpoint.

faq.question: Which authentication pattern does it describe?
faq.answer: It describes DefaultAzureCredential, which can use managed identity or configured developer credentials.

faq.question: Can it help with async clients?
faq.answer: Yes. It notes the async client option for higher throughput and concurrent application designs.

faq.question: Does it cover cleanup?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes deleting threads and agents when they are no longer required.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for Azure documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it as practical guidance and verify details against current SDK documentation.
